container_info.description:
The Recipe Book project is a digital platform that enables users to upload, manage, and share their own recipes, as well as receive personalized recipe recommendations. The system aims to foster a community-driven environment where culinary enthusiasts can discover new dishes, organize their favorite recipes, and interact with others. The platform will leverage user-generated content and recommendation algorithms to enhance user engagement and provide tailored suggestions based on preferences and past activity.

Expected outcomes include a user-friendly web and mobile application, robust backend services for recipe management and recommendation, and a scalable architecture to support future feature expansion.

steps.name: environment
steps.description: Prepare workspace, validate python3, pip, and python3-venv availability. Create workspace directories, a workspace-local .env file with restrictive permissions, and ensure created paths have appropriate ownership without broad chown on parents. Do not write global shims to /etc/profile.d to minimize global state.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/recipe-book-310206-310326/BackendServices"
[ -n "$WORKSPACE" ] || { echo 'WORKSPACE empty' >&2; exit 2; }
case "$WORKSPACE" in /*) ;; *) echo "WORKSPACE must be absolute" >&2; exit 2 ;; esac
# create workspace dir with correct ownership (avoid chown -R on parents)
sudo mkdir -p "$WORKSPACE" && sudo chown "$(id -u):$(id -g)" "$WORKSPACE"
# validate python3 and pip
command -v python3 >/dev/null || { echo 'python3 not found' >&2; exit 3; }
python3 -m pip --version >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo 'pip not available; ensure python3-pip installed' >&2; exit 4; }
# ensure python3-venv available, install non-interactively if missing
if ! python3 -m venv --help >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  sudo apt-get update -q >/dev/null && sudo apt-get install -y -q python3-venv >/dev/null
fi
# create dirs and workspace-local env file
mkdir -p "$WORKSPACE/data" "$WORKSPACE/logs"
ENV_FILE="$WORKSPACE/.env.backendservices"
TMP_ENV="$ENV_FILE.tmp"
cat > "$TMP_ENV" <<EOF
APP_MODULE=app.main:app
DATABASE_URL="sqlite:///$WORKSPACE/data/dev.sqlite"
CELERY_BROKER_URL=redis://127.0.0.1:6379/0
EOF
chmod 600 "$TMP_ENV"
if ! cmp -s "$TMP_ENV" "$ENV_FILE" 2>/dev/null; then mv "$TMP_ENV" "$ENV_FILE"; else rm -f "$TMP_ENV"; fi
# minimal checks for redis and uvicorn (non-fatal)
command -v redis-cli >/dev/null 2>&1 && redis-cli -h 127.0.0.1 ping >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
python3 - <<'PY' || true
try:
  import uvicorn
  print('uvicorn', getattr(uvicorn,'__version__','unknown'))
except Exception:
  pass
PY

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/recipe-book-310206-310326/BackendServices"
mkdir -p "$WORKSPACE" && cd "$WORKSPACE"
mkdir -p app/routes app/services app/models tests data logs
cat > "$WORKSPACE/app/main.py" <<'PY'
from fastapi import FastAPI
from app.routes import health, recommendations
app = FastAPI()
app.include_router(health.router)
app.include_router(recommendations.router)
PY
cat > "$WORKSPACE/app/routes/health.py" <<'PY'
from fastapi import APIRouter
router = APIRouter(prefix="/health")
@router.get("/")
def status():
    return {"status":"ok"}
PY
cat > "$WORKSPACE/app/routes/recommendations.py" <<'PY'
from fastapi import APIRouter
from app.services.recommendations import get_recommendations
router = APIRouter(prefix="/recommendations")
@router.get("/")
def list_recs():
    return {"items": get_recommendations()}
PY
cat > "$WORKSPACE/app/services/recommendations.py" <<'PY'
_data = [{"id":1,"text":"Try the tomato soup"}]
def get_recommendations():
    return _data
PY
cat > "$WORKSPACE/app/models/__init__.py" <<'PY'
# models placeholder
PY
# pinned compatible requirements (FastAPI 0.95.2 with Pydantic 1.10.12)
cat > "$WORKSPACE/requirements.txt" <<'TXT'
fastapi==0.95.2
pydantic==1.10.12
uvicorn
requests==2.31.0
pytest==7.4.0
httpx==0.24.1
# optional: psycopg2-binary (install separately if using Postgres)
TXT
cat > "$WORKSPACE/.gitignore" <<'TXT'
__pycache__/
.venv/
data/*.sqlite
.env.backendservices
logs/
TXT
# ensure sqlite file
SQLITE_FILE="$WORKSPACE/data/dev.sqlite"
if [ ! -f "$SQLITE_FILE" ]; then
  python3 - <<PY
import sqlite3,os
os.makedirs(os.path.dirname('$SQLITE_FILE'), exist_ok=True)
conn=sqlite3.connect('$SQLITE_FILE')
conn.execute('PRAGMA user_version=1')
conn.commit(); conn.close()
PY
fi
# start script
cat > "$WORKSPACE/start.sh" <<'SH'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/recipe-book-310206-310326/BackendServices"
cd "$WORKSPACE"
[ -f "$WORKSPACE/.env.backendservices" ] && . "$WORKSPACE/.env.backendservices"
VENV_PY="$WORKSPACE/.venv/bin/python"
if [ -x "$VENV_PY" ]; then
  exec "$VENV_PY" -m uvicorn ${APP_MODULE:-app.main:app} --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
else
  exec python3 -m uvicorn ${APP_MODULE:-app.main:app} --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
fi
SH
chmod 755 "$WORKSPACE/start.sh"
# test file
cat > "$WORKSPACE/tests/test_health.py" <<'PY'
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

def test_health_ok():
    client = TestClient(app)
    r = client.get('/health/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert r.json() == {"status":"ok"}
PY
# set permissions: created workspace owned by current user already; files 644, dirs 755
find "$WORKSPACE" -type d -exec chmod 755 {} +
find "$WORKSPACE" -type f -exec chmod 644 {} +
chmod 755 "$WORKSPACE/start.sh" || true

steps.name: validation
steps.description: Validate the environment: start the app via start-001, poll /health/ up to TIMEOUT with fixed interval, verify returned JSON via venv python, non-fatally check redis reachability, capture logs, and perform a clean shutdown.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/recipe-book-310206-310326/BackendServices"
cd "$WORKSPACE"
LOG="$WORKSPACE/logs/validation.log"
: > "$LOG"
# start via start step
bash -c "$WORKSPACE/$(basename start.sh 2>/dev/null || echo start.sh)" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
# If start step wasn't invoked externally, invoke start.sh via start-001 pattern
if [ ! -f "$WORKSPACE/logs/start.pid" ]; then
  setsid "$WORKSPACE/start.sh" >>"$WORKSPACE/logs/start.log" 2>&1 &
  echo $! > "$WORKSPACE/logs/start.pid"
fi
PID=$(cat "$WORKSPACE/logs/start.pid" 2>/dev/null || true)
# poll with fixed 1s interval up to TIMEOUT seconds
TIMEOUT=30
COUNT=0
until curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:8000/health/ -o /tmp/health.out 2>/dev/null || [ $COUNT -ge $TIMEOUT ]; do
  sleep 1; COUNT=$((COUNT+1))
done
if [ $COUNT -ge $TIMEOUT ]; then
  echo "server failed to respond within $TIMEOUT seconds" | tee -a "$LOG" >&2
  [ -n "$PID" ] && (PGID=$(ps -o pgid= $PID | tr -d ' ' 2>/dev/null) || true) && kill -TERM -"$PGID" 2>/dev/null || true
  exit 5
fi
# validate JSON using venv python if present
VENV_PY="$WORKSPACE/.venv/bin/python"
if [ -x "$VENV_PY" ]; then
  "$VENV_PY" - <<PY || { echo 'health-json-invalid' | tee -a "$LOG" >&2; rc=7; }
import sys,json
obj=json.load(open('/tmp/health.out'))
assert obj.get('status')=='ok'
PY
  rc=${rc:-0}
else
  python3 - <<PY || { echo 'health-json-invalid' | tee -a "$LOG" >&2; rc=7; }
import sys,json
obj=json.load(open('/tmp/health.out'))
assert obj.get('status')=='ok'
PY
  rc=${rc:-0}
fi
if [ $rc -ne 0 ]; then
  echo 'health validation failed' | tee -a "$LOG" >&2
fi
# non-fatal redis check
if command -v redis-cli >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  redis-cli -h 127.0.0.1 ping >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo 'warning: redis ping failed' | tee -a "$LOG" >&2
fi
# graceful shutdown
if [ -n "$PID" ] && ps -p $PID >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  PGID=$(ps -o pgid= $PID | tr -d ' ')
  kill -TERM -"$PGID" 2>/dev/null || true; sleep 1; kill -KILL -"$PGID" 2>/dev/null || true
fi
wait 2>/dev/null || true
echo "validation completed" | tee -a "$LOG"
